core_memory.academic_progress: transitioning from intro to advanced topics like algorithmic concepts, system design, and quantum computing basics
core_memory.class_interest: theory connecting to real-world problem-solving, e.g., pathfinding in large networks, handling huge datasets with minimal time complexity
core_memory.topics_covered: dynamic programming, approximation algorithms for NP-hard problems

archival_memory.course_distributed_systems: CS 2631, second hardest course, involves heavy reading, group discussions, and a major project simulating a decentralized file storage system
archival_memory.group_project_challenges: collaborating with peers having different coding styles and project ideas; handling concurrency issues and node failures
archival_memory.project_milestone: spending hours troubleshooting a bug caused by a misplaced bracket in a config file; achieving accomplishment after fixing the issue
archival_memory.elective_game_design: counts toward major when combined with specific classes; professor is industry veteran with experience in indie games; covers 2D/3D engines, physics implementation, and UX design
archival_memory.assignment_example: designed a labyrinth-based mini-game focusing on balancing difficulty curve to prevent player frustration; challenging but rewarding to develop
archival_memory.class_quantum_computing: Introduction to Quantum Computing; initially intimidating but now enjoyed; professor focuses on conceptual understanding with linear algebra and code examples in quantum circuit simulation frameworks; studying theoretical advantages of Grover's and Shor's algorithms over classical methods
archival_memory.capstone_project: end-of-year project using machine learning to analyze social media sentiment for emergency response; involves real-time detection of crisis indicators from tweets or posts; building an interface for city officials or campus security; integrates database management, API development, front-end design, and ML pipeline; includes project management with agile practices like sprints and daily stand-ups
archival_memory.elective_philosophy_of_mind: last required non-CS elective; explores consciousness, mind, and implications for AI; small class with focus on discussions; helps bridge technical knowledge with ethical considerations; wrote a paper on whether strong AI could ever experience qualia, such as subjective experiences of color or pain
archival_memory.class_schedule_mondays_wednesdays: 9:30 AM: Advanced Algorithms; short break; 11:00 AM: Distributed Systems lecture; after lunch: Capstone meetings(varied: lectures, lab work, team time)
archival_memory.class_schedule_tuesdays_thursdays: morning: Quantum Computing; afternoon: Game Design; Thursday evening: Philosophy of Mind
archival_memory.friday_schedule: no scheduled classes; spent on assignments, group projects, or labs; also engaged in undergrad research on data visualization for big scientific datasets
archival_memory.project_challenges: Capstone project consumes 10+ hours weekly, especially when encountering bugs or model training issues; Distributed Systems project also demands significant time; group meets at least twice a week; relies on Slack or Discord for coordination; scheduling five people is challenging but valuable for academic, hands-on learning without job pressures
archival_memory.overall_experience: transitioned from dreading tough CS classes to feeling confident in problem-solving and time management; occasional late nights due to debugging or deadlines; senior year has built confidence in resourcefulness, collaboration, and critical thinking; all coursework directly contributes to future career goals; finds the experience rewarding and personally fulfilling
